nodes.name: Molten Li reduction of NiO/G
nodes.procedure: The synthesis of the LiₓNiO/Ni heterostructure was performed inside an Ar-filled glovebox using presynthesized NiO/graphene with 60 wt% NiO as the starting materials (Figure 1a, S1). Typically, 20 mg of NiO/G was loaded together with 200 mg of Li metal in a 35 mL crucible, which was slowly heated to 250°C using a hot plate. Li slowly melts during this process and spontaneously reduces NiO via the redox reaction of NiO + Li → Ni + Li₂O. The molten mixture was maintained for 20 min and then cooled to room temperature. The solidified solid was transferred out of the glovebox.

nodes.name: Post-synthesis purification
nodes.procedure: The solidified solid was transferred out of the glovebox and immersed in 50 mL of ethanol for 24 h, which slowly leached off the excess Li and produced Li₂O/LiOH. The final catalyst powders were collected via filtration, washed with a copious amount of water, and tested directly as HER catalysts after vacuum drying.

nodes.name: Ni foam oxidation
nodes.procedure: Pristine Ni foam (porosity ~96%; area density ~300 g m⁻²) was first calcined in air at 600°C for 1 h to introduce a sufficient number of NiO layers (~5 μm thickness).

nodes.name: Ni foam molten Li treatment
nodes.procedure: NiO/Ni foam was then treated with molten Li using the same procedure as for graphene support (Figure 4b, S14). The treated Ni foam was still rigid, and SEM images revealed that the Ni backbones were coated with agglomerated particles, which are believed to have similar LiₓNiO/Ni heterostructures.

nodes.characterization_summary: BET specific surface area of 132 m² g⁻¹ with average pore size ~2.0 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The nitrogen absorption-desorption analysis revealed a typical IV isotherm, and the average pore size was ∼2.0 nm. The BET specific surface area was 132 m² g⁻¹, ∼50% higher than NiO/G (Figure S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern exhibits peaks only from crystalline Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction pattern of the produced catalyst exhibited peaks only from crystalline Ni (XRD, Figure 1b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Interconnected Ni nanocrystals 2-10 nm surrounded by 1-3 nm Li_xNiO nanoclusters with lattice spacing ~0.24 nm corresponding to NiO; abundant vacant defective sites in nanoclusters.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Specifically, the chemical lithiation produced interconnected Ni nanocrystals with sizes of 2−10 nm. These nanocrystals were surrounded by 1−3 nm nanoclusters with a lattice spacing of ∼0.24 nm that corresponds to NiO (Figure 1d-e).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS survey shows 4.27 atom% Li; O 1s peak at 532.0 eV (+2.0 eV shift); Ni 2p Ni²⁺ at 855.9 eV (+2.0 eV shift) indicating Ni-deficient defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray photoelectron survey spectra (XPS) revealed the presence of 4.27 atom% Li in the as-synthesized Li_xNiO/Ni... Li_xNiO/Ni exhibited a broad but well-defined O 1s peak at 532.0 eV... the Ni²⁺ binding energy also positively shifted by ∼2.0 to 855.9 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: Blue shifts of ∼33 cm⁻¹ in vibrational two phonon Raman scattering: 2TO mode at ∼730 cm⁻¹ and 2LO modes at ∼1090 cm⁻¹ due to phonon confinement around defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The heterostructures exhibited evident blue shifts of ∼33 cm⁻¹ in vibrational two phonon (2P) Raman scattering compared with NiO/G both for the 2TO mode at ∼730 cm⁻¹ and 2LO modes at ∼1090 cm⁻¹ (Figure 2c).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pronounced absorption peak at 534 eV assigned to unique oxygen species; shoulder below 530 eV indicates Ni³⁺ from Ni-deficient sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Li_xNiO/Ni catalyst is the only sample whose spectrum exhibited a pronounced absorption peak at 534 eV, which is assigned to the unique oxygen species active in the Li_xNiO/Ni catalysts.
